entries.note: Draws the dieline into an element; shows a hint when the type has no spec or the size is incomplete.
Returns the SVG text only.
Returns the flat (unfolded) width and height.

name: Dieline Engine (TMDieline)
purpose: Draws the flat dieline of a product type from its dimensions, live while Sales types the size.
inputs: The dieline recipe of the product type (prod_type.dieline_spec): canvas size, variables and a list of elements (cut, crease, bleed, hole) written as formulas.
The sizes typed on the form: product length (A), width (B), height (C), diameter, lid height, glue flap, tuck flaps, dust flap, overflow margin.
outputs: Cut lines red, crease lines green, bleed grey dashed, holes blue.
Width and height of the unfolded sheet, used by Pro-Dev as the starting size for imposition.
steps: Reads the short names (A, B, C, ...) and maps them to the form fields.
Evaluates every formula of the recipe with those values (plus, minus, times, divide, max, min, round ...). No geometry is hard coded.
Computes the canvas width and height; without a valid size nothing is drawn.
Draws each element of the recipe in order and returns one SVG.

entries.note: One plano, one flat size: the basic layout.
Level 1: tries every flap length in the allowed range and ranks the results.
Level 2: also tries the "69" interlock, the second copy turned 180 degrees and shifted.
Tool #2: tries all active standard planos and ranks them by paper used.
Tool #10: two parts of one product on the same sheet, compared with separate sheets.
Tool #4: running metres of cutting and creasing rule for the die.
Position of every piece on the sheet (mm), for the drawing.
Flat size = body plus flap on the chosen side.

name: Imposition Engine
purpose: Finds how many pieces (UP) fit on a plano sheet and which layout wastes the least paper.
inputs: Flat (unfolded) size of one piece in mm.
Strip the press needs to grip the sheet, in mm.
Free edge around the sheet in mm.
Allowed flap length range and the side the flap sits on (sweep tools).
Order quantity; when given, the best sheet is judged on the sheets really needed for it.
outputs: TEGAK (upright), PUTAR (rotated) or CAMPUR (main block plus a rotated block in the rest area).
Share of the usable area that is used / wasted.
Columns, rows and piece size per block: the data behind the drawing.
Usable area after margin and gripper.
combinePair only: COMBINED, SEPARATE or NONE, and the area saved per set.
steps: Usable area = plano minus margins and gripper.
Counts pieces upright and rotated; the higher count wins.
Tries the mixed layout: upright block first, then rotated pieces in the remaining strip; kept only when it gives more pieces.
Efficiency = area of all pieces divided by the usable area.
The sweep tools repeat this for every flap length (and shift), then rank by UP, then by efficiency.
The officer picks one of the top results. Nothing is saved by the engine.
writes: Nothing: pure calculation. The Pro-Dev screen saves the chosen layout to prod_layout_group.

entries.note: Calculates the three sections. Writes nothing.
Saves the result to the part; sections the officer overrode or typed by hand are left alone.
BOP and BOM for one Work Order quantity, from the layout Pro-Dev already saved.
Rows on the part that do not come from the engine (override / manual).

name: Spec Engine (BOP · BOM · Ink)
purpose: Builds the production specification of a part: process steps, materials and ink configuration.
inputs: The inquiry part: finishing, material, colour notation, quantity per pack, order quantity, artwork.
Layout decisions of Pro-Dev: sheet size, plano size, sheets per plano, press, die-cut machine, UP, order quantity, artwork colours.
Sections the officer changed (bop, bom, inks); null = follow the engine.
outputs: Bill of Process: steps in order with the suggested machine.
Bill of Material: material, quantity, unit, waste.
What is missing or unusual (no machine fits, no rule for a finishing ...).
The officer sections, normalised, ready to save.
steps: Reads the inquiry input and the layout decisions.
Applies the admin rules in prod_bop_rule to turn finishing and material into process steps and usage rates.
Calculates sheets, material quantities and ink per colour for the order quantity.
Returns the result with a source per row: ENGINE, OVERRIDE (officer changed it) or MANUAL (old / typed data).
On Save, only ENGINE sections are rewritten; "back to the engine result" removes an override.

entries.note: Runs monthly (prodev:usage-rates) or on demand.

name: Usage Rate Engine
purpose: Learns material usage rates and waste percentages from real production data and proposes new values for the BOP rules.
inputs: Start date of the production data to learn from.
true = write the proposals; false = only show them.
outputs: Per rule: current rate, proposed rate, sample size.
How many rules were changed automatically (only rules marked auto apply).
Size of the sample, the period and a remark when there is too little data.
steps: Proposed rate = current rate x (material really used / material planned).
Planned = quantity required on the Work Order; real = issued from the warehouse minus returned.
Waste per process = defect / (good + defect) from the production output records.
Below the minimum sample nothing is proposed.
Values typed by an officer are never overwritten; a rule is changed without asking only when it is marked auto apply.
writes: tm2mst.prod_bop_rule (proposal columns; the rate itself only with auto apply)

name: Routing Template Engine
purpose: Checks the order of process steps and turns a routing template into ready steps with a suggested machine.
inputs: Steps to check: process, sequence, branch. May be an unsaved draft.
The routing template to check or to apply.
Sheet length, sheet width, gsm: machines that cannot take the size are not suggested.
The product, to find the templates that fit it.
outputs: Order that is technically impossible (stripping before die-cutting).
Unusual order that still has real cases; never stops the officer.
Each step with the suggested machine and its resolved parameters.
Templates that fit the product; the default first, never chosen silently when there is no default.
steps: Compares each pair of steps with the precedence table.
For each step, picks a machine from the process x machine capability matrix that fits the sheet size and gsm.
Parameters come from three layers: the process x machine pair, then the machine, then the process default.

name: Costing Engine (Pro-Cost)
purpose: Calculates the cost price (HPP) of every part and the selling price per quantity tier of an inquiry.
restricted: The cost recipe is confidential (Costing and Directors only). This page shows the flow, not the formulas or rates.
inputs: The costing document (iqp_costing) with its parts, coatings and price tiers.
DC, DC+SF, DC+SHEET, KRAFT (offset family) or SHEET, SHEET_DIGITAL (corrugated).
Paper and grammage, print size, plano size, UP, coating, lamination, tooling, quantity per set, tolerance.
Quantity, tolerance, margin (non VAT and VAT), rounding step and mode.
Mode 1: pulled from the confirmed Pro-Dev layout. Mode 2: typed by the officer. Both must give the same HPP for the same geometry.
outputs: Paper, sheet, process, coating, lamination and tooling cost per piece, and the part total.
Total material, process and finishing cost per piece, and tooling for the order.
HPP per piece, price after tolerance, after rounding, after margin, and the price with VAT.
steps: Takes the main tier quantity as the base quantity.
Calculates every part with the rule of its type (offset family or corrugated).
Rolls the parts up to the header, weighted by quantity per set.
For every tier: adds tooling divided by that quantity, applies tolerance (rule differs per part type), rounding, margin and VAT.
Everything runs in one transaction; rates are frozen on the document, so later master changes do not move an old costing.

name: Reverse Costing
purpose: Turns a stand-alone (instant) costing into an integrated one by creating the documents that normally come before it.
inputs: An instant costing that has no inquiry yet.
outputs: A new inquiry of type NEW linked to the costing.
Created as Draft; only a person can Confirm it.
steps: Creates the Master Product and its parts (Draft).
Creates the inquiry and its parts and links them to the costing.
Creates the Pro-Dev layout as Draft.
The numbers of the costing do not change: the parts stay "typed by officer".

entries.note: Sends the document to the first step that matches; null = no active flow, the document stays where it is.
Approves the waiting step and opens the next one, or ends the flow.
Stops the flow; a reason is required.
Postpones the decision; the status does not change.
The approval queue of one user, including positions he is acting for.

name: Flow Engine (Approval)
purpose: Moves a document through its approval steps, the same way for every module.
inputs: Which flow: CO, PR, PO, AD ...
Status the document leaves (for example DRAFT).
Document value; steps can apply to a range of amounts.
Division, when the flow differs per division.
The step being decided and the reason (reject / hold).
outputs: The step now waiting and the position that must decide, or the final status.
Every action is written to the flow log: who, when, which step, the note.
steps: Finds the active flow configuration of the module (and division).
Picks the first step whose status-from and amount range match.
Finds who decides: the holder of the position, or the person acting for it within the acting dates.
Approve looks for the next matching step; none left = the flow is finished.
Steps of kind AUTO or NOTIFY ONLY are executed without waiting.

entries.note: Confirm on the screen = send the order to the approval flow; null = success, otherwise the message.
Runs when the last approval passes: the order becomes Confirmed and the schedule is created.

name: CPDEL Engine (Customer Plan Delivery)
purpose: Creates the delivery schedule when a Customer Order is confirmed.
inputs: The Customer Order with its lines.
Required on every product line before Confirm.
outputs: One line per product line: full quantity on the due date.
Submitted, then Confirmed after the last approval.
steps: Refuses when a product line has no due date (or, for an order without quotation, no Master Product), or when a product still has more than one quantity line to choose from.
Sends the order to the Flow Engine (CO).
After the last approval, creates one delivery line per product line that has no manual schedule yet.
Lines already scheduled by hand are not touched.
Sales can then Split or Join the lines on the CPDEL screen.

entries.note: Row colour by working days left to the slot.
Why a slot is not valid; empty = valid.
PPIC: when the goods will be ready; later than the slot needs a reason.
Sales: the new slot agreed with the customer, may split part of the quantity.
Sales: the customer refused, escalate to the Operational Manager.
Operational Manager: overtime, priority, subcontract or a new offer.

name: CPDEL Two Promises
purpose: Keeps the promise to the customer (delivery slot) and the promise of production (ready date) in line.
inputs: The form values of the action: date, time, reason, quantity to split.
outputs: WAITING_PPIC, ALIGNED, NEED_NEGOTIATION, ESCALATED, LATE or SHIPPED.
Past = red, today = orange, soon = yellow, shipped = grey.
Every action is recorded; the first promised date never changes.
steps: A slot is valid only inside Telasih office hours, the customer receiving hours and on a working day.
PPIC fills the ready date; when it is later than the slot the line asks Sales to negotiate.
Sales records the new slot (or a split) agreed by WhatsApp or phone.
A refusal goes to the Operational Manager, whose decision sends the line back to PPIC.

entries.note: The whole picture: every demand line and every material with its coverage.
Step 1: what must be made and when.
Step 2: the materials one demand needs.
Saves the proposed booking of a confirmed order (Draft, soft).
PPIC locks the booking: stock is reserved per location.
Back to Draft: stock is released and the plan recalculated.
Recalculates every order (button, nightly command, order changes).
PPIC chooses the stock item for a line that only has a specification.

name: Material Planning Engine (MPS · MRP · Booking)
purpose: Works out which materials every order needs, books stock for it and shows what is short.
inputs: Active Customer Orders: Confirmed = firm; Draft / Submitted = shown only.
The rest of the MPS forecast after the orders of the same month.
The earlier of the delivery date and order date plus the working days in BOOKING_NEED_WORKDAYS.
Available stock, open Purchase Orders and Requisitions with their dates.
outputs: Per demand and material: needed, covered by stock / PO / PR, short.
Per material: total need, available, first needed, order by (latest), coverage status.
One booking document per order (Draft or Confirmed).
steps: Finished goods stock of the same product is booked first.
The rest is broken down into all materials: paper from the Pro-Dev layout, then costing, then BOM; ink, varnish, coating, film and glue from the usage standards.
Netting per material: Confirmed first, then Draft, then Forecast, each by need date.
Supply is used in this order: available stock, PO on time, PR, late PO / PR, then SHORT.
A booking confirmed by PPIC is frozen: read from the database, not recalculated.
The engine only reads master data; it writes bookings and requisitions only.

name: Work Order Generation
purpose: Creates the Work Orders when a delivery line is posted to Production.
inputs: One delivery line of a Confirmed and approved Customer Order.
outputs: One per part of the product, with operations (routing) and materials. A product without parts gets one simple Work Order for PPIC to complete.
steps: Refuses when the line already has Work Orders, the order is not Confirmed and approved, or the line has no Master Product.
One inquiry part = one Work Order.
Operations and materials come from the Spec Engine for this quantity.
Target rates are taken from the product and part code.

entries.note: The waiting jobs of one machine, in order.
The job that should start now; null when its crew is not available.
Target start and finish per operation; not saved.
Checks a drag / resize on the board; empty list = allowed.

name: PDR Engine (Scheduling)
purpose: Decides which job a machine should run next and plans a Work Order backwards from its due date.
inputs: The crew PPIC wants to assign.
The moment to judge from (default: now).
The Work Order to plan backwards.
A manual move on the Scheduling Board.
outputs: Jobs or groups of jobs, highest priority first.
Target start and finish per operation.
Why a manual move is refused.
steps: Batching: jobs that can run together (same dieline ...) become one unit.
Priority score in layers: hot job, critical ratio, earliest due date, resource fit, first in first out.
Sequencing: smooths the order among jobs of equal priority only.
Crew check: the top job is skipped when its crew is not on shift.
Backward scheduling: from the due date back through the operations, using the rate band of each process and the machine calendar.

name: Scheduling Rule Engine
purpose: Applies the batching and sequencing rules kept as data, not as code.
inputs: The operations waiting for a machine.
The same list after the priority score.
The resource the rules belong to.
outputs: Lists of operations; a group of one = no batching fits.
The list reordered inside equal priorities.
steps: Reads the active rules of the resource.
Batching joins operations of different Work Orders that share the rule key.
Sequencing rules are applied oldest rule first as the main key, later rules as tie breakers.
The priority order (hot job, critical ratio, due date) is never changed.

name: Hot Job Option Generator
purpose: When an urgent job must be inserted, proposes up to three ways to do it with their measured impact.
outputs: One to three options; each shows which job moves, by how many hours, and whether it stays safe.
The option PPIC chose is recorded.
steps: Takes the waiting queue of the machine from the PDR Engine.
For the first two waiting jobs: "insert and move this job", with the delay in hours (the duration of the urgent job) and whether the moved job still meets its due date (safe / at risk).
Always adds a last option: send the urgent job to a subcontractor, so no job moves (needs a subcontract Purchase Order).
Shows the options; PPIC decides. There is no automatic answer.

name: Speed Target Engine
purpose: Proposes the target speed of every machine and of every process x machine pair.
inputs: Per machine: its data, its own output history and its process pairs.
The target filled in now (for the decision whether to propose).
outputs: A suggestion: speed, source, confidence (Low / Medium / High), sample size.
A suggestion per process x machine pair that has its own history.
steps: Sources are tried in order; the first that gives a number wins: v2 output, old-system output of the machine, old-system output of the process, same machine model, ratio to similar machines, the model specification, the process default.
Pass 1 uses the history of each machine; pass 2 lets machines without history borrow from the others.
A pair is proposed only from its own history; without it, it inherits the machine target.
PPIC is asked only when the target is empty, or the difference is larger than the minimum percentage with at least Medium confidence.
The engine never reads or writes the database itself: a repository loads the data, a store keeps the proposals as PENDING.
writes: tm2mst.prod_speed_suggestion (PENDING); targets change only when PPIC accepts.

name: Purchase Quotation Matcher
purpose: Matches the text of a supplier quotation file to the supplier master and to the requisition lines.
inputs: Supplier name as written in the file.
The lines of the requisition the quotation answers.
outputs: The requisition line or Material Master item and a percentage.
steps: Score = average of shared words (sizes and grammage count) and letter similarity.
First tries the requisition lines, then the Material Master.
A score below "sure" is marked yellow: the officer must choose.

entries.note: Builds or refreshes the register of one month; paid or filed rows are not changed.
Journal for the tax payment to the bank.
Records the filing reference.
Corporate income tax provision on the profit so far this year; only the difference is posted.
Register against ledger against source, for the status panel.

name: Tax Engine
purpose: Builds the monthly tax register (VAT, income tax 21 and 23), posts payments and reconciles with the ledger.
inputs: One register row to pay or file.
Payment date, state payment number and the bank account.
Who runs it and whether the data is live or dummy.
outputs: Per tax: base, tax, due dates, status.
Differences between register, ledger and source.
steps: Classify, calculate, post, reconcile, then pay and file.
All rates and due dates are read from the tax scheme table, so they change without code.
VAT payment nets output against input.

entries.note: May be repeated while the run is Draft or Calculated.
HR checks all employees or a random sample.
Locks attendance; refused while a payslip still has an anomaly.
Closes the period and opens the next one as an empty Draft.

name: Payroll Engine
purpose: Calculates the payslips of a period from attendance and takes the run through verification, payment and closing.
inputs: The payroll run being moved to its next status.
outputs: Draft, Calculated, Verified, Confirmed, Paid, Closed.
One per employee with its components.
An employee without an active salary rate stays visible and blocks Confirm.
steps: Loads the rule matrix (status, penalty, overtime) once per run.
Reads the daily attendance status of every employee in the period.
Builds each payslip: salary components, overtime per hour, deductions.
Verification, then Confirm locks attendance; Paid and Closed are status records.

name: Assistant Engine (offline)
purpose: Answers a question typed by the user without sending anything outside the company.
inputs: A help topic, for the "How to use" button.
outputs: A number, a help text, a screen to open, or "I do not know".
steps: Tries in order: a registered number whose phrase matches, help when the question has a question word, a screen, help without a question word, the local language model choosing among the closest candidates, then "I do not know".
Numbers come only from registered metric classes; the language model never calculates.
Help text is quoted from the help tables, never composed.
